author: BoldAndBrash
body:
Every time I join a game of Quintus, here is what i see... at least 5 people, usually donors stacking, with diamond armor in front of the other teams base, killing them right as they leave. Apparently, this is called "kill farming". Many people are probably hating me for requesting this. But when I play quintus, every single time the people who are getting "farmed" are getting mad in chat. They say things like "STOP SPAWNKILLING" or "OMFG YOUR CAMPING OUR SPAWN!" But even though this isnt what the farmers are doing, what they do is worse than spawnkilling. basically, the player leaves the spawn only to be ambushed by 100 diamond guys."Jus tunnel under and get iron" is probably what youre saying. but that isnt even possible. the diamond guys end up flooding the ENTIRE base, going on top of the spawn dome, the monuments, and the iron mines.


If you dont agree, please dont just say "-1" give reasons.

Of course. It's perfectly legal to kill somebody if they're trying to kill you, so long as you do not enter the opposing team's spawn or kill anybody inside it

Exception: 
Player A leaves his/her spawn
Player B attempts to kill player A
Player A retreats back to spawn for refuge

In this, and only this scenario, you are allowed to kill player A in spawn

replies.author: Riskayyy
replies.body:
Kill Farming is often providing a clear field of view over a choke point/spawn point or position of tactical interest whilst retaining position on the map. This can be done using traps, or gathering in groups.

This tactic allows one or many player/s to easily pick off any opponent that comes into sight.

It often proves frustrating, particularly to newer players, as it rewards those who invest a considerable amount of time in the game (which allows them to know the layout of the maps and the best options); as well as those who are good at PvP.

As long as you don't shoot or enter into the opposing team's spawn, it's completely legal.

@99: Staff members should always rank their Moderating over gameplay. If they see a report which needs to be reviewed, they should always leave to deal with it. If you see someone slacking off, contact a Senior Moderator+ with concerns/proof about him or her. 

EDIT: Oops, that wall of text was not directed at you, 99. Only the last paragraph was.
